name: Latvia: Part II package and CTIS upload check
applies_to: the Latvia package as a whole (plan-level checklist step)

items.check: K1 present on the Recruitment and Informed Consent Procedure template version 2.0, with the Latvian Member State fields and a section for every population pathway in the plan.
K2 Latvian recruitment material for every item used for participants or doctors.
Every population named in the protocol matches a Latvian information and consent document (L1 and the population-specific sets whose trigger is true).
L2 other participant-facing material; endpoint-related instruments in Part I with their Latvian translation in Part II on the CTIS translation route.
For every Latvian site: M1 dated CV, M2 declaration of interest, N1 signed and dated site suitability statement, P2 draft contract and budget.
O1 insurance certificate (and policy terms where needed) meeting Cabinet Regulation No. 192.
P1 compensation template present, also when no payment is offered.
R1 data-protection statement confirming GDPR and Latvian law.
S1 biological-samples statement.
Fee and proof of payment handled according to ZVA's current instructions (not stated in the guides).
Latvian used for participant-facing documents and for recruitment material intended for participants or doctors.
Administrative documents in Latvian or English as chosen (DECISIONS.md D1); M2 on the English template.
Any additional language version (for example Russian) matches the Latvian version in meaning, version and date, and is approved before use.
Site-suitability form signed and dated by the correct institutional representative before submission.
No signatures on K1, K2, L, M2, P1, P2, R1 and S1 uploads; blank consent forms unsigned; M1 dated.
Insurance limits and covered risks meet Cabinet Regulation No. 192 and match the participant documents.
Reimbursement wording aligned across the consent forms, compensation template (P1), contract and budget (P2).
Protocol number, EU CT number, sponsor, study centre and version consistent across all documents.
Data flows, recipients, transfers and retention identical in R1, the participant documents and the protocol.
Sample types, storage, transfers and retention identical in S1, the protocol and the participant documents.
Consent pathways in K1 match the L1 sets in the package.
Each Latvian site consistent across CTIS, M1, M2, N1 and P2.
Documents adapted from the reference package contain the Latvian national additions and no leftovers from the reference country.
items.applies_when: Latvia is not the reference package

items.check: Correct B-S section prefix and CTIS placeholder for each document.
Unique, self-explanatory title of at most 100 characters: <section code>_<document type>_<subtype>_<country>_<language>_<special attribute>.
Participant-document filenames identify the document type (adult, legal representative, 0 to 13 years, 14 to 17 years) and language.
Version and date in CTIS metadata, not in the title.
Personal names only where disclosure permits (principal investigator in M1/M2).
Clean, tracked-change, redacted or public and split-file variants clearly distinguished.
Uploaded filename base contains none of ( ) / , . ; | [ ] (the period before the extension is fine).
Article 11 workaround: every mandatory Part II placeholder holds the official placeholder PDF titled Part_II_placeholder_document_Article_11_workaround.
items.applies_when: Latvia receives Part I only under Article 11

items.check: For each document, publication status checked against the current Annex I publication tables (revised CTIS transparency rules applicable from 18 June 2024; ACT EU guidance v2.2, 30 April 2026).
Publishable documents: personal data and CCI identified separately; public version redacts only qualifying material.
Public and assessment versions differ only by the intended redactions; each in the correct CTIS slot.
No personal data or CCI in public structured fields.
No drafting instruction remains in any document (see content/conventions/template-instructions.md).
The Latvia patient-facing document QC checklist was run as the final content review of every participant document.
Every document approved by the owner in TrialAgents, or the user has explicitly chosen to export unapproved versions.
